findings.title: The Proposal card's Posting block render gate is unverified at the single-sentence arity, which is the modal case and #1352's own headline scenario
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutation `proposal.postingBlockSentences.length > 0` -> `length > 1` survives BOTH card tests that supply a Posting block (RT-M10, RT-M11). It is NOT an equivalent mutation: behaviour differs for exactly one sentence — the mutant renders nothing where HEAD renders the correction. It is NOT an unexecuted branch: both tests execute the gate, one at n=2 and one at n=1. The n=2 test asserts the sentences render; the n=1 test asserts only that Apply stays enabled, so nothing observes the n=1 render. A single-reason Posting block is the common production shape (JUDGE_ENABLED=false alone, or Copilot alone) and is precisely the scenario #1352 was filed for. The owner's recorded decision is 'card guaranteed, chat guided' — this is the guaranteed half, and its guarantee is unmeasured at its most likely arity. Production code at HEAD is CORRECT; the defect is in the test that claims this coverage. Fix is one line: assert the sentence renders in the existing single-sentence test, or render one sentence in the rendering test.

findings.title: The restore-card branch of the Posting block fix has no covering test, and its own comment names that risk
findings.arbiter_reasoning: restoreCardFacts threads the read context into policyCardFacts so a restore that re-arms auto-posting carries the correction; the code comment above it says 'a fix applied to only one branch leaves restore cards silent'. Neutering exactly that branch (passing an unblocked posting status) left all 56 tests in proposals.test.ts, ProposalCard.test.tsx, RestoreWorkflow.test.tsx and apply.test.ts green. No test in the repo asserts postingBlockSentences on a restore card — neither the mocked suites nor the two live-DB cases in reads.integration.test.ts. Recorded as an uncovered change (P1) rather than a confirmed survivor, because no candidate test exercises the behaviour at all.

findings.title: The directory page's prompt.ts row states a universal that is false: one of the five added rules is neither about the Posting block nor gated on correctionOwed
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The row reads 'Five rules state the **Posting block**, every one of them gated on `snapshot.posting.correctionOwed`' and then enumerates only FOUR. Machine check of prompt.ts at HEAD: five bullets were added; four contain the literal 'Posting block' and 'correctionOwed'; the fifth — 'Say "set to post", never "posts". A configured rule is a setting, not a guarantee...' — contains neither. It is an unconditional phrasing rule, not a gated one. The branch's own test encodes the correct scope (it filters to rules containing 'Posting block' before asserting correctionOwed), so the doc is out of step with the test beside it. Either the count is wrong or the universal is.

findings.title: A comment and fixture added on this branch assert a readiness behaviour that this branch's own ADR 0034 removed, and the fixture now models a state unreachable at HEAD
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The comment says 'readiness carries autopilot_unavailable (it folds in autopilotPurchasable(), which the runtime never reads)'. ADR 0034, landed on this branch, deleted that fold: buildReadiness now passes autopilotAvailable = tierGrantsAutopilot(tier) alone (settings.ts:1218). The branch corrected the same sentence in posting-status.ts, context.ts and the glossary but not here. The fixture is worse than stale: settings() pins readiness.blockReasons = ['autopilot_unavailable'] alongside posting = { blocked: false, reasons: [] }, and at HEAD autopilot_unavailable implies !tierGrantsAutopilot, which forces autopilot_tier_required into posting.reasons and blocked = true. No account can produce that response. The test still passes and still checks a valid structural property, but its stated discriminator no longer exists; posting-status.ts itself now names provider_moderation_not_validated as the surviving one.

findings.title: Absence-of-one-literal proxy stands in for 'no reason code leaks to the owner'
findings.arbiter_reasoning: `expect(screen.queryByText('judge_disabled')).not.toBeInTheDocument()` is commented as 'no reason code leaking to the owner', but it only excludes one of five literals, and it passes trivially because the card is handed owner sentences and never a reason code — the card has no reason value to leak. Behavioural replacement: assert the rendered list equals the supplied sentence array exactly (which also catches an extra or reordered line), or iterate every AutoApprovalPostingBlockReason key. Recorded, not blocking.
